Shader library

Small shaders to study, each with what it costs and where it fits.

Depth fade

Softens where a sprite meets the ground, so smoke does not show a hard line.

TranslucentCheap

Fresnel rim

Lights the edges of a surface that face away from the camera.

OpaqueCheap

Flow map water

Moves a normal map along a painted flow, so rivers bend around rocks.

OpaqueMedium

Parallax occlusion

Fakes depth by marching a height map in the pixel shader.

OpaqueHeavy

Dissolve

Clips pixels by a noise value that rises over time, with a glowing edge.

MaskedCheap

Refraction

Bends what is behind glass or water by offsetting the scene colour.

TranslucentMedium

Reading a cost

"Cheap" means a few instructions per pixel. "Heavy" means a loop or many texture reads per pixel.

The real cost depends on how much of the screen the material covers. A heavy shader on a small decal can cost less than a cheap one on the whole sky.

Notes in a scroll box

This box scrolls on its own. A selection inside it must stay on its text when the box scrolls, and must not show outside the box.

Parallax occlusion steps along the view ray through a height map. More steps look better and cost more.

Most games use 8 to 32 steps, and fewer steps at a distance, where the detail cannot be seen.

Silhouettes stay flat, because the trick only moves where the texture is read, not where the surface is.

Tessellation or real geometry is needed when the edge of the surface must change shape.

float3 flow = (tex2D(FlowMap, uv).rg * 2.0 - 1.0) * FlowStrength; float phase0 = frac(Time * Speed); float phase1 = frac(Time * Speed + 0.5); float3 n = lerp(SampleNormal(uv + flow * phase0), SampleNormal(uv + flow * phase1), abs(phase0 - 0.5) * 2.0);
